title: Artificial Intelligence in Middle and Secondary Education: Instructional Opportunities, Limitations and Ethical Considerations
content: Middle and secondary school educators should utilize and implement Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a support tool for instruction, not a replacement for their pedagogy and lesson planning. Utilizing and implementing AI can assist with lesson planning, differentiation, feedback, and generating learning materials; and its uses should be guided by clear expectations, professional judgment, and school policy. Educators should also teach their students how to use AI ethically, verify outputs for accuracy and bias, and protect student privacy by avoiding sensitive data. Most importantly, assessments should be designed to show genuine student understanding, with AI used transparently and appropriately. The best available published advice concurs that the usage of AI within an educator’s pedagogy significantly enhances middle and secondary school students’ learning. This article offers practical guidance for educators who use or plan to use AI in the classroom, while also highlighting policy recommendations to support effective educational practices.
